newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Egypt hoping to clinch Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Egypt hoping to clinch Hebron deal.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Sunday that Egypt was trying to close a deal between the PLO and Israel on a partial Israeli pullout from Hebron.
"There are some Egyptian efforts concerning this issue," Arafat told reporters in Gaza when asked if a deal could be signed at a Middle East economic conference in Cairo scheduled for November 12.
PLO officials said their leadership would like to sign an agreement in Cairo to complete an Israeli troop evacuation from parts of the West Bank city.
"We have to reach agreement first," PLO negotiator Hassan Asfour said.
U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross left the region on Tuesday after failing to broker a deal between the two sides held up because of Israeli security demands.
Arafat sent negotiators Saeb Erekat and Hassan Asfour to Cairo on Saturday to report to the Egyptians on the talks.
PLO officials said Egypt offered to help narrow the gaps.
The PLO accuses Israel of delaying an agreement by introducing changes to the deal signed last year between the PLO and the former Israeli government. Israel blames the PLO.

Arafat said the main obstacles to a deal were Israeli demands, rejected by the Palestinians, such as the type of weapons Palestinian police would carry in PLO-controlled areas in Hebron, the reopening of the al-Shuahada (martyrs) street in the heart of Hebron used by Palestinians and Jewish settlers, and other security issues.
"We now have the same situation, nothing has been changed," Arafat said. Some 400 Jewish settlers live and study in the heart of the city, home to 100,000 Palestinians.
